closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Both the prohibition of being clever about one's work and the warning against self-glorification in distress were read. The first clause's particular force was not resolved by a generic work or humility passage, so the unit remains incomplete.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit reasons that one honored in poverty is more honored in wealth, and one without honor in wealth more so in poverty. The available texts mention poverty and wealth as coming from the Lord, as things to avoid, or in generosity, but none makes this comparison of honor across the two states.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The two comparisons intensifying honor or dishonor between poverty and wealth were read. No independently supported target reproducing that particular social comparison was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit introduces a man who grows rich through attention and frugality and the 'reward' allotted to him. The texts about storing treasure for unknown heirs or the rich fool share the outcome described in the following verse, not this unit's method of accumulation by attention and frugality, and the remaining texts share only the words rich or reward.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The accumulation of wealth through attention and frugality and the introduction of its allotted reward were read with the following death warning. The retained parallel for 11:19 does not independently establish this unit's particular method of accumulation.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit forbids saying, 'What need do I have, and what good things will be mine from now on?' The available texts share only the word 'mine' in unrelated statements about silver and gold, seats in the kingdom, or Job's speech, and none expresses the same question.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The questions about present need and future good were read. Their force was not flattened into the unambiguous complacency of the following verse, and no particular target resolving that wording was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says an hour's suffering makes one forget luxury and that a person's works are revealed at his end. The available texts concern the house of mourning, Jesus' rejoicing in an hour, sufferings and coming glory, or the end of those who forget the Lord; none joins forgetfulness of luxury with works revealed at death.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The hour of suffering that erases luxury's memory and the disclosure of works at life's end were read. No actual target establishing this combined observation was retained; general death or judgment texts were insufficient for its distinctive claim.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit warns that a stranger settled in one's house brings disorder and estranges one from one's own people. The available texts describe a crooked man separating friends, a disorderly retreat, or disorder in a church, and none concerns a stranger lodged in the household.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The settled stranger bringing household disorder and estrangement from one's own people was read. No named outsider or other hospitality warning was identified as this specific causal scenario without supporting text.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit warns against placing an enemy beside oneself or at one's right hand lest he seek one's seat. The available texts describe the seating and station of Solomon's attendants, Christ seated at God's right hand, or a kinsman declining redemption, and share only the words station, seat or right, not this succession danger.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The warning against placing an enemy beside oneself or at one's right hand lest he take one's place was read. No particular succession narrative was assigned to that scenario without a text establishing the same relationship and positioning.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit describes a wealthy associate who lives with someone who has means and empties him while taking no trouble himself. The available texts share only the words empty, trouble or take in unrelated contexts such as returning the ark, Daniel's preservation or Gehazi's greed.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The wealthy associate living with and draining someone who has resources while taking no trouble was read. Other passages about grudging meals or abandoned friendship do not establish this particular depletion arrangement.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit warns against being misled or brought low through one's folly. The available texts speak of prophets misleading the people, assumptions misleading many, idolatry not misleading, or the folly at Gibeah, and share only the words misled or folly.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The warning against deception and humiliation through folly was read within the wealthy-associate sequence. No additional passage-grounded relationship specific enough to that contextual warning was retained; a generic admonition against folly was not counted.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit urges great vigilance because one walks alongside one's downfall. The available texts use 'take great care' or 'keep watch' for keeping the law or seeking wisdom, or describe Jesus walking on the sea, and none concerns walking beside one's downfall.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The urgent vigilance required while walking alongside one's downfall was read in the courtly-danger context. No particular independent target was retained beyond broad danger language.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says every living creature loves its like and every person his neighbor. The available texts mention sea creatures, a creature molded from clay, or a one-horned creature, and share only the word creature, not the principle of loving one's like.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The comparison of creatures loving their like with persons loving a neighbor was read. It was not equated without qualification with a command to love neighbors or creation's taxonomic kinds; no particular counterpart was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says all flesh gathers according to kind and a man clings to someone like himself. The available texts distinguish kinds of flesh or describe flesh consumed or preserved, but none states the principle of social affinity among like persons.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The gathering of all flesh by kind and human attachment to similar people were read. The actual Genesis creation-by-kind language does not itself state this social-affinity principle, and it was not used as a substitute.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit declares no one worse than the one who begrudges himself and introduces the repayment of his evil. The available Proverbs texts warn about dining with or the haste of a begrudging man toward others, and the remaining texts share only the words begrudging or repayment; none concerns begrudging oneself.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The superlative judgment upon one who begrudges himself and introduction of his evil's repayment were read. The related self-harm passages do not independently support this precise superlative and transition.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says the self-begrudging man does good forgetfully and in the end reveals his evil. The available texts concern forgetting luxury in suffering or being a forgetful hearer of the law, and share only words of forgetting and revealing, not this conduct.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Doing good forgetfully and finally revealing evil were read. The unusual adverb was not replaced with hypocrisy or an asserted intention that the text does not state; no supported independent counterpart was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says God did not have mercy on 'the nation of destruction, those carried away in their sins' without naming that nation. The Deuteronomy texts concern Israel showing no mercy to the nations of Canaan or their destruction for ungodliness, which would require supplying an identification the unit does not state, and the other texts share only words such as destruction, carried or sins.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The unnamed nation of destruction carried away in sins was read. No nation was supplied by assumption from the surrounding examples, and no target was retained that would require that unresolved identification.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says there is a tempest a person will not see and most of God's works are hidden, within the speech of one who thinks God takes no notice. The Job texts speak of hearing little of God's ways and of thunder and great deeds not known, and the psalms mention tempests in other senses; none shares the unseen tempest or this argumentative setting.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The unseen tempest and hidden divine works were read within the exchange ending in a verdict of foolish reasoning. Job's different account of limited knowledge was examined, but no link was retained that could obscure this passage's argumentative role or assert the same unseen tempest.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says God set His eye upon human hearts to show them the greatness of His works. The available texts praise the greatness of God's works, the heavens recounting His glory, or His invisible qualities seen in creation, but none describes God setting His eye upon hearts.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The supplied wording says God set His eye upon their hearts to show His works' greatness. It was preserved without substituting familiar wording about fear; no actual target explaining this precise eye-upon-hearts gift was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is the paradox that when a person finishes he begins and when he stops he is at a loss. The available texts ask what man is, describe finishing a work, or use 'at a loss' in other settings, and none shares this paradox.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The paradox says finishing is beginning and stopping leaves one at a loss. General statements about unsearchable divine works do not independently establish this precise sequence, so the source is deferred without adding an explanatory subject to its wording.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says every understanding person has known wisdom and will give acknowledgment to the one who finds her. The available texts speak of God making wisdom known or teaching wisdom, but none concerns acknowledgment given to the one who finds wisdom.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The unit specifically joins knowing wisdom with acknowledgment of the person who finds her. The read texts about acquiring wisdom do not establish this particular acknowledgment relationship.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says only that the one who rejoices in heart will be condemned. The available texts concern the condemnation of Jesus, condemnation of unbelievers, or the heart condemning us, and none shares this statement about rejoicing in heart.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The native text says the one rejoicing in heart will be condemned. It does not explicitly say rejoicing in sin; a link based on that added qualifier would silently alter the source.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit contrasts a gift that does not benefit with a gift whose repayment is double. The available texts mention rulers loving gifts and repayment, Joseph's brothers taking double silver, or the Corban gift, and none shares this contrast between profitless gifts and double return.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The contrast includes both a gift without benefit and a gift repaid double. The read warnings about grudging gifts do not substantiate the distinctive double-repayment clause or settle its direction.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says someone buys much for little and pays for it sevenfold. The available texts share only the words much, little or someone in unrelated statements, and none describes a purchase repaid sevenfold.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Buying much for little and paying sevenfold is a particular reversal in exchange. Neither ordinary debt warnings nor the read theft-restitution text establishes that this purchase is theft or an equivalent transaction.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says those who eat the fool's bread are base in speech and asks how many will laugh at him. The available texts concern eating the Lord's bread, a stone base under the Sea, or practicing base things, and share only the words bread or base.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The unit describes the fool's bread-eaters as base in speech and asks how many laugh at him. General warnings about foolish speech do not establish this particular relationship between the host, guests, and mockery.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says someone makes a promise to a friend out of shame and gains him as an enemy for nothing. The available texts speak generally of a friend becoming an enemy, friendship with the world, or acquiring things, but none involves a promise made from shame.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source links shame-induced promising with acquiring a friend as an enemy. It does not specify a financial guarantee; the read warnings about pledges cannot safely be substituted for its unspecified promise.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit contrasts one known far away for power of tongue with the understanding person who knows when he slips. The available texts speak of slips of the tongue, intelligible speech, or wisdom known through speech, but none shares the contrast between distant fame and recognizing one's own slip.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The contrast pairs far-reaching fame for powerful speech with the understanding person's recognition of his own slip. A general tongue warning does not independently support that particular fame-and-self-recognition contrast.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says wisdom is like a ruined house to a fool and an uncomprehending person's knowledge is unexamined words. The available Proverbs texts contrast wise and foolish speech or conduct in general terms, and none shares the ruined-house comparison or the unexamined words.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Wisdom as a ruined house to the fool and knowledge as unexamined words form a distinctive comparison. The read house-building images concern stability or destruction, not this exact description of how the fool regards wisdom.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says that when an ungodly person curses Satan he curses his own soul. The available texts refer to Satan tempting Jesus, divided against himself, or taking away the word, and none concerns cursing Satan or cursing one's own soul.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The explicit claim that the ungodly person cursing Satan curses his own soul requires an explanatory relationship not stated here. General warnings about cursing do not establish that self-directed consequence.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says that if evil befalls the speaker because of a friend, everyone who hears will guard against him. The available texts describe guards at the crucifixion or tomb, reports of an outrage, or people glorifying God at what happened, and share only the words guard, hear or happen.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source specifically predicts public caution about a friend after others hear of harm suffered because of him. The read loyalty and betrayal texts do not establish that particular report-and-warning sequence.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit speaks of 'an expression comparable to death' to be kept from Jacob's inheritance without naming it. The law on naming the Lord's name would require identifying that expression as blasphemy, which the unit does not state, and the other texts share only the words inheritance, depart or sins.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The expression comparable to death is not named in this unit. It was not identified as a particular oath or blasphemy without textual support, and generic condemnation of bad speech is insufficient.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is only the numerical introduction 'Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring wrath'. It names no sin itself, and the available texts on adultery, sexual immorality, ordered gifts, or multiplied sins and wrath relate only to the examples that follow or share only the counting form.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: This native unit is the numerical introduction to the examples that follow. It names no particular sinful conduct by itself; an unrelated three-part list would provide only a formal resemblance.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit states preferences for any wound but a wound of the heart and any evil but a woman's evil. No text in the edition was found that makes the same comparisons; passages on marital trouble or grief do not share the stated preferences.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The hyperbolic preferences single out a heart wound and a woman's evil. Neither the read passages about marital damage nor faintheartedness matches the stated comparison closely enough to retain a distinct pair.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit continues with preferences for any calamity but that from those who hate, and any retribution but that of enemies. The available psalms ask rescue from enemies and those who hate, or lament defeat by them, and share only those common terms, not the comparison of calamities.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The repeated preferences intensify calamity from haters and retribution from enemies. General enemy passages do not establish these particular comparisons with every other calamity or retribution.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit ranks a snake's head and an enemy's anger as unmatched extremes. The Proverbs sayings concern living with a quarrelsome wife, and the other passages only share the words anger and enemy; none uses the snake's-head comparison or ranks anger this way.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The snake's head and an enemy's anger are set out as unmatched extremes. No read target sufficiently connects those specific comparisons, and the head was not silently changed to venom.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit's distinctive image is a woman's evil darkening her face like a bear. The Daniel passages describe faces changing from fury or fear, Leviticus concerns a lesion's appearance, and Proverbs 27:15 uses a dripping image; none has the bear comparison.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The image specifically makes a woman's evil alter her appearance and darken her face like a bear. General facial-expression or marital-conflict passages do not support the distinctive bear comparison.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says that wrath, shamelessness and great shame result when a wife supplies her husband. Sirach 26:8 concerns a drunken wife, Sirach 22:4 concerns a daughter, and the Chronicles verses concern Israel's repentance; none addresses a wife's provision for her husband.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The particular claim attaches wrath and shame to a wife supplying her husband. The read passages about harmful marital conduct do not establish this claim about provision itself.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit pairs giving water an outlet with giving an evil wife freedom of speech. Proverbs 17:14 in this edition has no water image. The other passages use freedom or freedom of speech in unrelated senses (before God, Christian liberty, national independence).
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The paired prohibitions concern an outlet for water and freedom of speech for an evil wife. The actual Proverbs 17:14 contains no opening-water image, and a broad speech warning would not establish the source's specific comparison.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says a third tongue drove out courageous women and deprived them of their labors. The leads only share isolated words (third, tongue, courageous, labor, deprived), with no saying about slander expelling women or taking their labors.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source specifically describes a destructive tongue expelling courageous women and taking their labors from them. No independently checked target for those particular social losses was retained; a generic warning about harmful speech would obscure the details.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit calls the death brought by the tongue an evil death and says Hades is preferable to it. The leads use the word preferable in unrelated comparisons (hope of resurrection; a thief and a liar) and do not compare a death with Hades.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source ranks the tongue’s evil death below Hades. No checked target establishes this particular comparison; broad sayings preferring death to hardship were not counted as a match.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit describes the grievous life of going from house to house as a guest who cannot open his mouth. The leads share only the words grievous, house, live or guest, in unrelated settings; none describes a dependent guest forced into silence.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source describes the humiliation and enforced silence of moving between others’ homes as a dependent guest. No checked target sufficiently matches that combination of dependence and loss of voice.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit names rebuke about lodging and a creditor's reproach as burdensome to a prudent person. The leads use the words burdensome or prudence about commandments and wisdom; none concerns lodging, debt or a creditor.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The target describes a creditor seizing bedding after an unpaid pledge; the source names reproach over lodging and debt, without that seizure. Linking the two as one concrete outcome depended too much on inference, so the pair and source completion were withheld.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit prefers a healthy poor person to a rich person scourged in his body. The Proverbs sayings share the better-poor-than-rich form, but their contrast is moral (truth versus lying, righteousness versus deceit), not physical health. The other leads do not make this comparison.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source specifically contrasts bodily health in poverty with bodily affliction in wealth. Ecclesiastes 6:2 concerns inability to enjoy possessions and calls it a grievous sickness, without establishing that physical-health contrast; the broader resemblance was not retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit contrasts the poor laborer's diminished livelihood and his neediness at rest with the rich laborer before him. The leads speak of the poor and needy in general (not depriving them, injustice to them, God hearing them) and do not describe this outcome of labor and rest.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The poor laborer remains needy even when resting, in contrast to the rich laborer in the preceding verse. No checked target adequately matches that unequal result of labor and rest.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit compares a mocking friend to a breeding horse that neighs under every rider. Jeremiah 8:6 compares a runner to a neighing horse, Jeremiah 9:4 speaks of mocking a friend, and the other leads mention friends or horses separately; none combines them in this comparison.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The mocking friend is likened to a breeding horse neighing under every rider. No checked target sufficiently establishes this particular comparison of friendship and indiscriminate responsiveness.

closed_source_units.reason: Re-reviewed with fresh leads; the proposed link did not survive a second reading: No textual connection: no shared wording, image or person, only a thematic application of Sirach's general advice to the parable. The father in Luke divides property and does not give his son authority over him.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source counsels retaining lifetime authority and money rather than becoming dependent on relatives or friends. No checked target supporting this complete specific precaution was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit urges preeminence in all one's works and keeping one's glory free of blemish. The Hezekiah passages concern setting a house in order before death, which is not this verse's subject, and the New Testament leads use blemish of sacrificial or moral purity before God.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The source calls for preeminence in one’s works and protection of personal glory. General praise of a good name was not counted as a specific checked parallel.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit describes a dream vision as a likeness of a face opposite a face. Proverbs 27:19 in this edition says faces are not like faces, which is the opposite of a mirror image. The other leads mention dreams, visions or likenesses without this face-to-face image.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The dream described as a face facing its likeness was read. Mirror passages were not substituted for this particular description without establishing how its set-against wording functions; no supported independent target was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit is the speaker's personal claim that his wandering showed him many things and that his understanding exceeds his words. The leads only share the word exceed, in unrelated contexts (righteousness, divine anger, fire in water).
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The speaker's extensive wandering and understanding exceeding his words were read. The preceding travel-and-learning comparison does not independently establish this autobiographical claim or the particular excess of understanding over speech.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says a twisted heart gives grief and an experienced person will repay it. Sirach 34:9 and 25:6 praise experience without the twisted heart or repayment. 2 Timothy 4:14 concerns the Lord repaying Alexander, and Ecclesiastes 2:1 concerns testing pleasure.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The twisted heart causing grief and the experienced person's repayment were read. The object and force of repayment were not supplied from a different revenge or counsel passage; the unit remains without a sufficiently precise counterpart.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit asks who will trust a well-girded robber springing from city to city. The leads mention robbers or thieves in unrelated settings (night thieves in Obadiah, a den of robbers, Jesus arrested as a robber), and Deuteronomy shares only the word springing.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The question about trusting a well-girded robber springing from city to city was read with the following unsettled-person analogy. No named traveler or robber was assigned to this particular portrayal without supporting text.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit asks evil thought where it rolled in from to cover the dry land with deceit. Genesis 6:5 and Jeremiah 17:9 speak generally of the evil or depth of the human heart. The others share only cover, deceit or dry land; none uses this image of evil thought covering the land.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The apostrophe asking where evil thought came from to cover the land with deceit was read. General accounts of temptation do not establish the particular origin and world-covering image, and no independent target was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit describes a companion who labors with a friend for his belly's sake and takes up a shield before battle. The Kings verses concern God shielding Jerusalem, and Proverbs 22:24 and Micah 7:5 warn about companions generally; none describes this self-interested companion.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The companion's labor for his belly and taking up a shield before battle were read. The shield action was not silently assigned a motive, beneficiary or outcome absent from the wording; no precise target was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit warns that a counselor will counsel for himself and may cast a lot against you. The leads concern the counsel of the ungodly, God needing no counselor, foolish royal counselors and divine counsel; none describes a self-interested advisor or the casting of a lot.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The warning to learn a counselor's needs lest he counsel for himself and cast a lot against the hearer was read. The self-interested advice example retained for 37:7 does not independently establish this unit's needs-and-lot detail.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit lists people with a conflict of interest who should not be consulted, such as a woman about her rival or a merchant about exchange. The leads only mention household slaves, hired workers or merchants in laws or sayings about how to treat them, not about consulting them.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The full list of interested or ill-suited counselors was read, including merchant, buyer, hired worker and household slave. A generic warning against foolish advice would not establish these specific conflicts or deficiencies, so it was not counted.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says a man's soul can report more than seven watchmen on a watchtower. Proverbs 20:27 and 1 Corinthians 2:11 speak of the human spirit's inward knowledge without the watchmen comparison. The other leads mention watchmen or reports in unrelated narratives.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The soul's reporting more than seven elevated watchmen was read. A general inward-discernment text would not establish this quantitative watchtower comparison; no precise target was retained.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says the preceding speaker was not given grace by the Lord because he was deprived of all wisdom. Luke 2:40 and 2 Corinthians 1:12 pair grace and wisdom positively and do not speak of grace withheld for lack of wisdom. The other leads share only the word deprived.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The statement that the preceding speaker lacks divine grace because he has been deprived of wisdom was read. The social-rejection contrast retained at 37:20 does not establish this specific causal judgment about grace and wisdom.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says God's works will not end and that peace on the earth comes from Him, in the context of healing and the apothecary. Luke 10:34 shows wound care without this statement, and the Jeremiah and Ezekiel verses concern war and peace in the land.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The continuation about God's works never ending and peace upon earth was read within the healing-and-compounding sequence. No particular target was retained that combines this continuing beneficial work with the stated peace without importing a different setting.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says there is a time when success is also in physicians' hands. The leads concern the Lord granting success in battle or Jason's misguided success, not success in medical practice.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The statement that there is a time when success also lies in physicians' hands was read with their ensuing prayer. General healing accounts do not identify this specific qualified allocation of success to medical practitioners.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says grief remains in calamity and the poor person's life weighs on the heart. The leads mention calamity in prayers, explanations of judgment or a psalm of protection, with no reference to lasting grief or the poor person's life.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Grief remaining in calamity and the poor person's life weighing upon the heart were read. No independently grounded target matching this particular conjunction was retained; broad sorrow language was insufficient.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit asks how a plowman occupied with oxen and bulls can become wise. 1 Kings 19:19 and Job 1:14 merely show oxen plowing, Ecclesiastes 12:11 uses goads as an image for wise words, and 1 Chronicles 20:5 mentions a spear shaft; none addresses a farmer's lack of leisure for wisdom.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The full rhetorical question about a plow-holder's opportunity for wisdom amid ox-driving and talk of bulls was read. The examined Isaiah agricultural analogy does not explicitly assign its divine-instruction clause to the farmer in this edition, so familiar wording was not substituted to manufacture a counterpart.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says a city cannot be settled or people sojourn and walk about without the craftsmen just described. The leads share only without, neither or sojourning (Lamentations, Hebrews 7:3, 1 Corinthians 11:11, Esther 4:16) and say nothing about craftsmen sustaining a city.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The necessity of the described craftsmen for a settled city and people's movement was read. The examined Ecclesiastes statement about cultivated land and a king did not establish this specific city-and-crafts dependency.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit speaks of spirits created for retribution whose scourges God made firm in anger. The psalm verses describe winds, fire and weather obeying God's word without any retributive role, and the other leads share only maker, anger or strength.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: Spirits created for retribution and prepared to assuage their Maker's anger were read. The unit does not name their identity; an examined psalm's angels, winds and fire were not equated with them without specific textual support for that identification.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says that when he opens his hands he will rejoice, while transgressors will cease. The unnamed subject is not identified as a generous giver, so Deuteronomy 15:11 (opening one's hand to the poor) cannot be matched to him. The other leads share only open, rejoice or transgressors.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The opened hands, rejoicing and complete cessation of transgressors were read as given. No unnamed agent was identified as God or a charitable giver merely to attach a generic hand-opening passage.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit says waterside reed grass will be plucked out before all other grass. Job 8:12 in this edition says every plant withers before it drinks, which is not a before-other-grass comparison. The other leads mention reeds, riverbanks or grass in unrelated settings.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The water-side reed being plucked before all other grass was read with the preceding ungodly-root image. The actual Job 8 wording does not make the same before-other-grass comparison; no equivalent was supplied from a familiar alternative text.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit ranks the green growth of a crop above grace and beauty desired by the eye. The leads describe green growth or fruitful trees as God's provision but do not compare them with beauty or grace.
closed_source_units.previous_deferral_reason: The ranking of green crop growth above grace and beauty desired by the eye was read. Genesis 2 combines beautiful trees and food but does not make this particular ranking, so the aesthetic-agricultural resemblance was not credited.

closed_source_units.reason: The unit lists, among things to be ashamed of, wronging the truth of God and His covenant and planting the elbow on bread. Job 31:1 and Matthew 5:28 concern looking at a woman, which is not part of this unit. The other leads share only the words bread, truth or covenant.
